column3: US1: Detect presentation attacks at login (print, screen, replay)
column5: As a user logging in, I want the system to confirm that a live person is in front of the camera so that nobody can enter my account with my printed photo, a photo on a screen or a replayed video. | Acceptance criteria: Print, screen and replay attacks are rejected in the demo; APCER, BPCER and ACER are reported per attack type on the held-out test set. | Story owner: Dinh Phu Nguyen (M1). Backup: the other member.

column3: US2: Clear camera guidance and status messages
column5: As a user, I want clear camera guidance and status messages so that I know how to pass the check and what to do when it fails. | Acceptance criteria: Distinct messages for success, spoof suspected, low quality (dark, blurred, no face, several faces), timeout and technical failure; a retry button. | Story owner: Dinh Phu Nguyen (M1). Backup: the other member.

column3: US3: Versioned subject-disjoint dataset split with frozen test set
column5: As a data engineer, I want a versioned, subject-disjoint dataset split with a frozen test set so that model comparisons are fair and experiments are reproducible. | Acceptance criteria: Manifest under DVC; automated check finds no subject overlap; test-set hash recorded before tuning. | Story owner: Dinh Phu Nguyen (M1). Backup: the other member.

column3: US4: Compare and select the PAD model on validation data
column5: As an ML engineer, I want to compare candidate models on validation data so that we select the model with the lowest attack acceptance inside our latency budget. | Acceptance criteria: At least three models logged in MLflow; threshold chosen on validation; comparison table with APCER/BPCER/ACER and Pi latency. | Story owner: Dinh Phu Nguyen (M1). Backup: the other member.

column3: US5: Run the anti-spoofing check on the Raspberry Pi
column5: As a device operator, I want the anti-spoofing check to run on the Raspberry Pi so that face images never leave the device and the check stays fast. | Acceptance criteria: INT8 ONNX model runs on Pi 5; inference p95 <= 50 ms per frame and <= 2 s per attempt; no images stored; result signed. | Story owner: Dinh Phu Nguyen (M1). Backup: the other member.

column3: US6: Rate limiting, privacy-safe logging and fail-closed behaviour
column5: As a security administrator, I want attempts to be rate-limited, logged without face images, and to fail closed so that attackers cannot brute-force or bypass the check and incidents can be audited. | Acceptance criteria: Retry limit and lockout work; logs hold decision, score, model version, error code and timestamp only; a technical failure never results in a login. | Story owner: Dinh Phu Nguyen (M1). Backup: the other member.

column3: US7: Monitoring and drift alerts that trigger retraining
column5: As an ML engineer, I want monitoring and drift alerts that trigger retraining so that the model stays reliable when lighting, cameras or attack types change. | Acceptance criteria: Weekly drift report (PSI) and audit APCER/BPCER tracked; retraining rules documented and dry-run once. | Story owner: Dinh Phu Nguyen (M1). Backup: the other member.
